191:     """
192:     # Use our universal function to load in the events
193:     events, labels = load_delimited(
194:         filename, [float, str], delimiter=delimiter, comment=comment
195:     )
196:     events = np.array(events)
197:     # Validate them, but throw a warning in place of an error
198:     try:
199:         util.validate_events(events)
200:     except ValueError as error:
201:         warnings.warn(error.args[0])
202: 
203:     return events, labels
204: 
205: 
206: def load_intervals(filename, delimiter=r"\s+", comment="#"):
207:     r"""Import intervals from an annotation file.  The file should consist of two
208:     columns of numeric values corresponding to start and end time of each
209:     interval.  This is primarily useful for processing events which span a
210:     duration, such as segmentation, chords, or instrument activation.
211: 
212:     Parameters
213:     ----------
214:     filename : str or `os.Pathlike`
215:         Path to the annotation file
216: 
217:     delimiter : str
218:         Separator regular expression.
219:         By default, lines will be split by any amount of whitespace.
220: 
221:     comment : str or None
222:         Comment regular expression.
223:         Any lines beginning with this string or pattern will be ignored.
224: 
225:         Setting to `None` disables comments.
226: 
227:     Returns
228:     -------
229:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n_events, 2)
230:         array of event start and end times
231: 
232:     """
233:     # Use our universal function to load in the events
234:     starts, ends = load_delimited(
235:         filename, [float, float], delimiter=delimiter, comment=comment
236:     )
237:     # Stack into an interval matrix
238:     intervals = np.array([starts, ends]).T
239:     # Validate them, but throw a warning in place of an error
240:     try:
241:         util.validate_intervals(intervals)
242:     except ValueError as error:
243:         warnings.warn(error.args[0])
244: 
245:     return intervals
246: 
247: 
248: def load_labeled_intervals(filename, delimiter=r"\s+", comment="#"):
249:     r"""Import labeled intervals from an annotation file.  The file should consist
250:     of three columns: Two consisting of numeric values corresponding to start
251:     and end time of each interval and a third corresponding to the label of
252:     each interval.  This is primarily useful for processing events which span a
253:     duration, such as segmentation, chords, or instrument activation.
254: 
255:     Parameters
256:     ----------
257:     filename : str or `os.Pathlike`
258:         Path to the annotation file
259: 
260:     delimiter : str
261:         Separator regular expression.
262:         By default, lines will be split by any amount of whitespace.
263: 
264:     comment : str or None
265:         Comment regular expression.
266:         Any lines beginning with this string or pattern will be ignored.
267: 
268:         Setting to `None` disables comments.
269: 
270:     Returns
271:     -------
272:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n_events, 2)
273:         array of event start and end time
274:     labels : list of str
275:         list of labels
276: 
277:     """
278:     # Use our universal function to load in the events
279:     starts, ends, labels = load_delimited(
280:         filename, [float, float, str], delimiter=delimiter, comment=comment
281:     )
282:     # Stack into an interval matrix
283:     intervals = np.array([starts, ends]).T
284:     # Validate them, but throw a warning in place of an error
285:     try:
286:         util.validate_intervals(intervals)
287:     except ValueError as error:
288:         warnings.warn(error.args[0])
289: 
290:     return intervals, labels
291: 
292: 
293: def load_time_series(filename, delimiter=r"\s+", comment="#"):
294:     r"""Import a time series from an annotation file.  The file should consist of
295:     two columns of numeric values corresponding to the time and value of each
296:     sample of the time series.
297: 
298:     Parameters
299:     ----------
300:     filename : str or `os.Pathlike`
301:         Path to the annotation file
302: 
303:     delimiter : str
304:         Separator regular expression.
305:         By default, lines will be split by any amount of whitespace.
306: 
307:     comment : str or None
308:         Comment regular expression.
309:         Any lines beginning with this string or pattern will be ignored.
310: 
311:         Setting to `None` disables comments.
312: 
313:     Returns
314:     -------
315:     times : np.ndarray
316:         array of timestamps (float)
317:     values : np.ndarray
318:         array of corresponding numeric values (float)
319: 
320:     """
321:     # Use our universal function to load in the events
322:     times, values = load_delimited(
323:         filename, [float, float], delimiter=delimiter, comment=comment
324:     )
325:     times = np.array(times)
326:     values = np.array(values)
327: 
328:     return times, values
329: 
330: 
331: def load_patterns(filename):
332:     """Load the patterns contained in the filename and puts them into a list
333:     of patterns, each pattern being a list of occurrence, and each
334:     occurrence being a list of (onset, midi) pairs.
335: 
336:     The input file must be formatted as described in MIREX 2013:
337:     http://www.music-ir.org/mirex/wiki/2013:Discovery_of_Repeated_Themes_%26_Sections
338: 
339:     Parameters
340:     ----------
341:     filename : str or `os.Pathlike`
342:         The input file path containing the patterns of a given piece using the
343:         MIREX 2013 format.
344: 
345:     Returns
346:     -------
